newsitem.title: USA: Coastal Aruba plant plans major turnaround in Sep.
newsitem.headline: Coastal Aruba plant plans major turnaround in Sep.

text.p: Coastal Corp's refinery on the Caribbean island of Aruba in Netherlands Antilles will undergo a major maintenance in September, according to a source familiar with the plant's operations.

"There is a major turnaround planned for September," said a Coastal source familiar with the plant's operations in Aruba. "It will shut most of the plant," he said, though he couldn't be specific about the dates.
A Coastal spokesman in Houston declined to comment on planned maintenance.

The Aruba plant, Coastal Corp's largest, with a capacity of 210,000 barrels per day (bpd), is a major supplier of feedstocks for gasoline-making units in the U.S. Gulf and Caribbean region. It makes naphtha and vaccuum gas oil, jet, diesel and "number six" heating oil, as well as small amounts of liquified petroleum gases, such propane and butane.
Coastal Aruba also was a major buyer of Iraqi crude oil during the first round of oil sales under the United Nations-sponsored "oil-for-food" deal, which ran from December 10 to June 7.
Coastal was among the largest single buyers during the period, lifting some 60,000 bpd over the first 180 days, all of which was shipped to the Aruba plant, traders said.
"They were taking VLCCs of it. Now, if they don't take it, it will be an even tougher sell for the Iraqis," said a Gulf crude oil trader.

After a two-month delay in starting its second round of oil sales, Iraq is expected to resume crude exports in early August. But having delayed, Iraq will be required to sell around $1 billion of oil by early September, meaning it will have to find buyers for between 1.5 million and two million bpd during that period or forego some of its allowed exports.
The Coastal turnaround, if it leads to curtailed purchases for Iraq's second round, could exacerbate Baghdad's problems in selling its oil in the next month or so, oil traders said.
